claims.text: Setting the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service enables Terraform and OpenTofu to use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.

`PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is an environment variable of the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service that specifies the domain that serves the Terraform-compatible API (for example `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`).
When `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is unset on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the DNS record for the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` domain should point at the same host that serves `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN`.
A separate domain for `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` is not required in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud: `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` can be set to the same value as `PULUMI_API_DOMAIN`, so no second DNS record is needed.

The Terraform/OpenTofu state backend guide (/docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/) uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.

For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the `PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN` value should be used in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login` or `tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name in place of `tf.pulumi.com`.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Terraform state backend for Pulumi Cloud.
Pulumi Cloud can serve as a state backend for both Terraform and OpenTofu.
